Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing for a preflight review ahead of Acme's internal control board (target week of Nov 20) and had a few clarifying asks so we can scope the artifacts we need from Redwood. High level: we need an ISO 27001 Annex A mapping into the CAIQ/SIG controls and a small set of sample artifacts that show the mechanics (logs, KMS attestations, snapshot extraction). Specifically: 

- Can you confirm whether you have an Annex A -> CAIQ mapping already (we need the mapping file, even if draft)?
- For FedRAMP preflight: what are your "evidence windows" for log retention snapshots (how far back can you pull consistent snapshots for auditor sampling)?
- Are there existing examples of log-extraction scripts or runbooks we can review (especially for KV cache evictions, tokenization logs, and k8s audit trails)?
- SOC 2 scope: will SOC 2 be co-termed with the ISO work or treated separately (our procurement expects a single cadence ideally)?

If easier, we can jump on a 30-minute sync; otherwise, a short reply with owners and timelines is fine. Looping in Lena from AuditOps — she may join the preflight.

Best,
Sam
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Inc

Hi Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front and a proposed plan below. Attached are two artifacts to start (ISO_Annex_Map_v0.2.xlsx and our FedRAMP_Preflight_Checklist.pdf) — both drafts but sufficient for scoping.

Quick answers:
- Annex A -> CAIQ: we have a draft mapping (attached) that aligns Annex A controls to comparable CAIQ control identifiers. It is still in review but covers the core control sets (A.5–A.18).
- Evidence windows / snapshots: operationally we can produce consistent snapshots for 90 days of application logs and 12 months for infra-level audit logs; for FedRAMP sampling we can produce a 30-day fine-grain extraction within 2 business days and a broader 90-day bundle within 5 business days.
- Log-extraction runbooks: we have scripts and a short runbook; Rishi is attaching a control-trace bundle after this reply.
- SOC 2 cadence: we typically align SOC 2 reporting separately but can coordinate timelines — if you prefer one cadence we can co-term the scope and deliver a single intake window.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dry-run preflight call (30m) — suggested Nov 10, 11am PST — to walk the mapping and checklist.
2) Action owners: Rishi — artifact samples and runbook; Priyom — CAIQ/SIG response matrix; Karthik — retention confirmation from infra region teams.
3) Deliverables: updated Annex map + runbook by Nov 8; sample extraction (30-day) by Nov 14.

If that plan works I'll calendar the Nov 10 slot and include AuditOps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: ISO annex convergence + FedRAMP preflight questions

Marissa / team —

Following up with technical detail and what's feasible for the timelines above. Quick notes and assumptions first: we assume Acme will only request tenant-level logs tied to the public API and admin plane (not full node cores).

- Retention and snapshots: application-level request logs are stored in our hot index for 30 days, then rolled to warm storage for 90 days (searchable). Infra k8s audit logs are retained 12 months in object storage with immutable snapshots for 90 days. For a 30-day fine-grain extraction we can provide a time-window consistent CSV export with associated hashing.
- Runbooks & extraction: attaching control-trace-examples.zip — it includes an extraction script (extract_logs.py), a sample k8s-audit slice, and a README with hash verification steps. Note: keys to note — we sanitize PII tokens and redact live prompt contents before handing off.
- KV cache & tokenization logs: we do not persist raw KV cache contents; we persist eviction events and metrics (timestamped) and function-level traces (no raw prompt content). We can surface the eviction event logs and correlating request ids.

Open questions for Acme: do you need raw request payloads (we will redact) or only event/metric traces? That changes the packaging and approval flow.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: control-trace-examples.zip (zip)]

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifications: 

- We do need the Annex A -> CAIQ mapping specifically to tie ISO clauses to CAIQ questions; the attached draft looks like a good start.
- Regarding request payloads: we need event/metric traces + request ids only; we prefer redacted payloads but the request id linkage is critical so our sampling can pull full threads if needed during the on-site.
- For SOC 2: co-terming would be ideal. I'll propose co-term in our procurement thread and can share dates if you want them to align.

Lena — can you confirm whether AuditOps needs any additional artifacts beyond the 30-day extraction runbook and the Annex map before the Nov 10 dry-run?

On the runbook: can you optionally include a short section that shows the hash verification output format (i.e., sha256sum) so our intake engine can validate integrity on arrival?

Appreciate the speed — confirm Nov 10 works (11am PST).

Sam
Director, Security & Compliance, Acme Inc
